G4: material outcome — the experiment exists to answer whether memory selectivity changes real task outcomes, not scores
question: Does the retrieval selectivity measured in S6-2 convert into material outcome on real work (G4) — fewer errors (M2) and less redundant re-discovery (M3), with M1 tokens/wall as the cost line — when the selective pi-lcm tool-level surface and the firehose claude-mem surface each serve live work sessions against the no-memory baseline?
baseline: the charter's locked baselines (Patch 3): the long-context null and the two pi-lcm baseline arms, plus the S6-2-measured claude-mem firehose arm as the contrast surface; primary comparisons are matched pairs under SPEC-OUTCOME-PROTOCOL.md M1-M3 with the stale-use penalty applied
stopping_rule: Run until 8 matched pairs per arm are complete; stop early if either memory surface regresses stale-use or M2 errors against the no-memory baseline on 3 consecutive pairs; if after n=8 the M3 redundant-re-discovery counts cannot separate the selective surface from the firehose, report cannot-distinguish as the completed result rather than extending.
why_this_one: S6-2 established the instrument can tell selective from indiscriminate retrieval and measured the arms 0.600 / 0.500 / 0.250 mean set-F1; this experiment tests the next link in the G4 chain — whether that instrument-level separation shows up as outcome-level separation on matched real work
